newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's left hurts Zedillo's PRI in state vote.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's left hurts Zedillo's PRI in state vote.

text.p: Mexico's left dealt a heavy blow to President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) by winning at least a dozen towns in a weekend state election, early official results showed on Monday.
Sunday's vote in the rural state of Morelos south of Mexico City was a key test for the PRI ahead of congressional and governors' elections in July.
Zedillo's party had previously dominated the state's political map, holding 32 of the 33 town halls and a big majority in the state congress.

But the state electoral commission said the 860,000 registered voters now looked set to give victory to the left-leaning Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) at least 13 towns, against at least 15 for the PRI.
Adding to the PRI's distress, the state capital Cuernavaca appeared to have fallen to the conservative National Action Party (PAN), which previously had no mayors in Morelos.
No official information was immediately available about the other four town hall races or the race for the state legislature.
The PAN won 34 percent of the vote in Cuernavaca, against 31 percent for the PRI and 20 percent for the PRD in early results, the State Electoral Institute said.

PAN leaders were quick to claim victory in the state capital. "This is very gratifying to see as it confirms the rebound of the PAN ... (in Cuernavaca)," the president of the PAN, Felipe Calderon Hinojosa, said in a television interview.
But the performance of the PRD, whose election results have been overshadowed by the PAN and the PRI in other recent votes, was especially notable in Morelos.

PRD voters gave the party a stunning 64 percent in the town of Tepoztlan, where the PRI mayor sparked violent protests in 1995 by backing a controversial development including a golf club and industrial park.
The PRI trailed with 24 percent and the PAN had a paltry 1 percent in early results, local station Radio Red said.

In the state's third biggest city, Cuautla, the PRD had won exactly half of the votes counted. The PRI had 29 percent and the PAN 8 percent. Radio Red added the PRD also was ahead in the cities of Yautepec, Zacatepec and Jojutla.
"With no fear of making a mistake, the triumph has been without question for the PRD candidate in Cuautla," PRD president Manuel Lopez Obrador told reporters.

Despite fears of violence, the elections in Morelos took place without major incident, although TV station Azteca reported late on Sunday that gunmen had been spotted driving around one town threatening voters from a car.
Late Thursday, unknown assailants threw paint thinner in the face and broke the nose of the ruling PRI's mayoral candidate for the city of Cuernavaca.
Voters gave Zedillo's PRI a tough time in the polls in 1995 and 1996, punishing it for the country's dire economic crisis and numerous corruption scandals.
Under an aggressive new national leader, Humberto Roque Villanueva, the PRI had hoped for better times in Morelos.
But analysts said the negative publicity surrounding PRI state governor Jorge Carrillo Olea had hurt the party.

Carrillo was accused by the New York Times of links to drugs traffickers, a charge he vigorously denied. Carrillo's government also suffered from citizen protests against a wave of kidnappings in the state. Some victims alleged state police were involved in the crimes.

Once home to peasant leader Emiliano Zapata, who led a famous revolt during the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution, Morelos is now better known as the state that media reports say contains two homes of the country's most wanted drug lord, Amado Carrillo Fuentes.
